tagline: Your repo. Your agent. Your harness.
hero_description: MetaHarness: your repo, your agent, your harness. A layered rotating torus and orange trajectory introduce a factory for custom agent harnesses.
intro: Follow the complete MetaHarness workflow: analyze a repository, generate an owned harness, connect a host, enforce policy, use memory and routing, evaluate changes, and ship a package.
cta:
[Open the Studio](https://ruvnet.github.io/metaharness/) · [Read the user guide](USERGUIDE.md) · [Explore MetaHarness](https://cognitum.one/metaharness)

```bash
npx metaharness --wizard
```

chapters.title: Begin with your repository
chapters.subtitle: Read the shape of the project before generating tools.
chapters.footer: DETERMINISTIC ANALYSIS · NO REPO CODE EXECUTED
chapters.summary: Repository analysis produces a recommendation before scaffolding.
chapters.body: `harness analyze-repo` reads repository structure and recommends a harness. Analysis does not execute repository code. Inferred build and test commands are emitted with execution disabled until explicitly trusted and enabled.
chapters.description: Begin with your repository. Repository analysis produces a recommendation before scaffolding.

chapters.title: Compose the agent you need
chapters.subtitle: Choose identity, tools, skills, policy, and a host.
chapters.footer: YOUR NAME · YOUR BRAND · YOUR CLI
chapters.summary: The generator turns project choices into a harness you own.
chapters.body: Use the Studio or CLI wizard to select a starting template and a host. The generated project contains agents, skills, commands, tool adapters, scoped memory configuration, governance, and provenance. Trim anything your repository does not need, then customize the package identity and behavior.
chapters.description: Compose the agent you need. The generator turns project choices into a harness you own.

chapters.title: One shared kernel
chapters.subtitle: Host-specific adapters surround reusable primitives.
chapters.footer: THE HARNESS CHANGES. THE KERNEL IS SHARED.
chapters.summary: Generated harnesses consume a shared Rust kernel through host adapters.
chapters.body: The generator produces an owned harness. That harness consumes `@metaharness/kernel`, whose Rust implementation is distributed through WASM and native bindings. Host-specific behavior belongs in adapters; the kernel does not depend back on a host. The kernel supplies reusable governance, memory, routing, and witness primitives.
chapters.description: One shared kernel. Generated harnesses consume a shared Rust kernel through host adapters.

chapters.title: Bring your preferred host
chapters.subtitle: Claude Code, Codex, RVM, and other host adapters.
chapters.summary: The same generated harness connects through distinct host adapters.
chapters.body: Choose the host integration your workflow needs. Claude Code and Codex use MCP surfaces; other hosts can use native extensions, skills, or CI configuration. Not every host supports MCP or the same policy controls. Prime Agent emits a sandbox-required runbook when a non-empty deny-list cannot be enforced by the host itself.
chapters.description: Bring your preferred host. The same generated harness connects through distinct host adapters.

chapters.title: Give tools a policy boundary
chapters.subtitle: Select the adapter mode and review its permissions.
chapters.summary: Tool permissions, approval rules, timeouts, and audit belong to policy.
chapters.body: The MCP adapter supports off, local stdio, and authenticated remote modes. Generated policy starts with restrictive defaults and exposes the permissions and limits for review. `harness mcp-scan` performs static checks for risky grants, missing audit or timeout settings, and other policy problems; it does not run the target tools.
chapters.description: Give tools a policy boundary. Tool permissions, approval rules, timeouts, and audit belong to policy.

chapters.title: Keep context scoped
chapters.subtitle: Project memory is part of the harness you configure.
chapters.footer: FIELD MEMORY IS OPTIONAL AND EXPERIMENTAL
chapters.summary: Project memory and optional field memory have different setup requirements.
chapters.body: The scaffold carries a memory namespace scoped to your harness. Experimental field memory is a separate, opt-in feature with deployment requirements for storage, a compatible adapter, and an authenticated principal verifier. It does not open storage or accept shared updates until those prerequisites are satisfied. Its illustrated vector geometry is a visual metaphor.
chapters.description: Keep context scoped. Project memory and optional field memory have different setup requirements.

chapters.title: Route against your quality bar
chapters.subtitle: Learn model choices from your own evaluation results.
chapters.summary: The router selects the cheapest candidate predicted to meet the quality bar.
chapters.body: `@metaharness/router` consumes query vectors and labeled evaluation examples. It predicts candidate quality and selects the cheapest model predicted to clear your configured threshold; if none does, it returns the best predicted candidate and reports whether the bar was met. The picture is illustrative and makes no universal quality or savings guarantee.
chapters.description: Route against your quality bar. The router selects the cheapest candidate predicted to meet the quality bar.

chapters.title: Evolve the harness
chapters.subtitle: Propose, test, evaluate, and retain measured improvements.
chapters.footer: THE MODEL STAYS FROZEN; THE HARNESS EVOLVES
chapters.summary: Darwin evaluates harness changes behind sandbox and safety gates.
chapters.body: Darwin Mode proposes changes to the harness, tests them in a sandbox, and keeps improvements that pass its evaluation and safety gates. The model stays frozen. Generated projects expose `npm run evolve`; no-network, no-API-key defaults support bounded refactoring and tuning. Changes still need evidence; animation is not a benchmark.
chapters.description: Evolve the harness. Darwin evaluates harness changes behind sandbox and safety gates.

chapters.title: Make releases reviewable
chapters.subtitle: Checks and provenance travel with the generated harness.
chapters.summary: Validation and evidence connect generated files to a reviewable release.
chapters.body: Generated provenance records what was produced. Doctor and validation commands help keep a customized harness healthy. The repository documents CI gates for kernel tests, generator checks, security, and deterministic signed witness manifests. Consult those gates and current CI for evidence rather than treating an animated status as a test result.
chapters.description: Make releases reviewable. Validation and evidence connect generated files to a reviewable release.

chapters.title: Ship it under your name
chapters.subtitle: A generated project becomes your own npm package.
chapters.footer: YOUR TEAM RUNS YOUR VERSIONED HARNESS
chapters.summary: Customize, validate, then publish the package under your chosen scope.
chapters.body: Rename and configure the generated project, keep the agents and tools your repository needs, validate it, and publish under your own package name or organization scope. Publishing is an explicit maintainer action. Consumers then use the versioned CLI you own; the generator does not silently publish a package for you.
chapters.description: Ship it under your name. Customize, validate, then publish the package under your chosen scope.

chapters.title: Explore governed extensions
chapters.subtitle: Advanced experiments keep explicit evidence boundaries.
chapters.footer: EXPERIMENTAL PATHS REQUIRE THEIR OWN GATES
chapters.summary: AVO, field memory, and ARC experiments have separate validation boundaries.
chapters.body: AVO adds governed variation with budgets, rollback, quarantine, and replay receipts. ARC and field-memory packages remain experimental and have their own deployment and evidence requirements. The stronger AVO-class claim is gated on its preregistered unseen-task evaluation; ARC results are not claim-eligible until the documented controlled-ablation gate passes. Weight-EFT is a separate, optional model-tuning path, distinct from frozen-model Darwin evolution.
chapters.description: Explore governed extensions. AVO, field memory, and ARC experiments have separate validation boundaries.

chapters.title: Mint your first harness
chapters.subtitle: Use the wizard, or generate a coding harness directly.
chapters.footer: OPEN THE STUDIO OR START FROM YOUR TERMINAL
chapters.summary: Create a named harness with the CLI and inspect the generated project.
chapters.body: Run the wizard for guided choices, or use a template and host explicitly. The example below generates `my-bot` for Claude Code; select `--host codex` for Codex. The Studio provides a browser workflow, and the user guide explains the generated files and commands.
chapters.description: Mint your first harness. Create a named harness with the CLI and inspect the generated project.
chapters.command:
npx metaharness my-bot --template vertical:coding --host claude-code
cd my-bot
npx . --help
